rationale:
Evidence: seven of eight designs ended off-track in all 60 trials per design, with max_error at 0.060 to 0.066 m whatever the gain, ki, span, mass or speed. The best score is 39.81 (iterations 3, 5 and 6, which are the same design apart from ki). Iteration 7 (wheel_track 0.10) lowered oval progress from 0.1675 to 0.115, so narrowing the track is not the answer.

Critique: I accept most of it. (1) My draft claimed speed was untested. It has been swept from 0.8 to 1.6, with no effect on max_error, so I drop the speed-only test. (2) The draft changed kp, kd, base_speed and geometry together, so no outcome could be attributed. I drop that. (3) Base 0.6 would cut ground speed in a 3 s run, and progress is time-capped, so I reject it. (4) kd 1.0 gives a sensor-edge derivative kick of about 50 turn units per step, with no oscillation to damp, so I keep kd at 0.1. (5) The critique's most likely cause, a fixed early departure, cannot be changed with the tools here. The untested drivetrain factor is wheel_radius (only 0.03 so far), which sets ground speed per PWM count. It is the lever most likely to move progress within the 3 s limit.

Kept: the best-tested layout (five sensors at x -0.032 to +0.032, y 0.05, size 0.012, weights -1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1), wheel_track 0.14, mass 0.8, body unchanged, last_direction, and the iteration-6 controller (kp 1.5, ki 1.0, kd 0.1, base 1.0). Changed: wheel_radius 0.03 to 0.04, the only variable that differs from the best run.

Expected result (hypothesis): higher ground speed per PWM, so oval progress should rise above 0.1675 at similar max_error. If max_error stays at 0.061 to 0.066 with unchanged timing, the cause is the start transient, and I will accept the best-tested design rather than keep sweeping. Success threshold: a score above 39.81. If steering_oscillation exceeds 0.25, the larger wheel is too aggressive, and the next step is wheel_radius 0.035.
